messages:
Maria Chen: Quick thread — need a compact plan for graceful-degradation routing for A/B + auto-shift. Question: should the fallback decision live in the control plane or the edge agent?
Jasper Reid: my 2c: keep final switching in the edge agent. Control plane pushes policies, but edge should make the fast call (latency + offline resilience).
Kevin Patel: agree on edge decisioning, but we need a tiny policy language. e.g. `if p50>200ms or error_rate>0.05 -> route-fallback`. Policies must be readable and versioned.
Sophie Alvarez: also need a safe default when policy mismatch happens (old agent vs new policy). fallback to a conservative pass-through route, not a full switch.
Maria Chen: good point. Proposal: policy carries `grace_mode` enum: {conservative, optimistic, force}. Agents default to conservative on parse failure.
Jasper Reid: +1. How do we validate live to avoid flip-flop? we should require a probe window and a min-stable-duration, e.g. 60s sample and 5m lock.
Kevin Patel: and add hysteresis: only allow 1 auto-shift per 10m per route, plus backoff multiplier. prevents thrashing under noisy signals.
Sophie Alvarez: telemetry implications: need per-agent local counters + periodic rollup to control plane. keep the rollup cheap: counts, p50/p95, error numerator/denom. no full traces required.
Maria Chen: ops-bot: create an alert if rollups stop for >2 minutes.
ops-bot: Alert rule created: `agent_rollup_missing > 120s` -> notify #eng-oncall.
Jasper Reid: state reconciliation: when control plane revokes a policy (rollback), agents should drain new traffic and keep existing sessions pinned for `session_ttl` (configurable). default 30s.
Kevin Patel: edge case: model variant incompatibility. If agent routes to variant B but model not present, agent must fallback to last-known-good variant and emit a `variant-mismatch` event.
Sophie Alvarez: cost tradeoff: fallback to larger but cheaper model vs smaller expensive one — ops must be able to rank by cost/quality. policy should accept `priority=[latency,cost,quality]`.
Maria Chen: final checklist from this thread to turn into RFC follow-up:
- minimal policy schema (conditions, grace_mode, hysteresis, session_ttl, priority)
- agent behavior matrix (parse-fail, mismatch, offline, probe-fail)
- rollup telemetry spec (metrics + cadence)
- safety knobs (rate-limit auto-shifts, manual lockouts)
- test harness: simulated noisy signals + canary path to verify non-thrashing
- backward compatibility: policy version negotiation and conservative default
Jasper Reid: I'll draft the policy proto and an agent pseudo-impl this week.
Kevin Patel: I'll mock up the telemetry rollup and alert rules.
Sophie Alvarez: I'll add the cost/quality ranking UI notes for Console.
Maria Chen: awesome, thanks. tagging @eng-sre for visibility.
triage-bot: Note: creating follow-up ticket INF-4821 for "Edge-first degradation routing policy RFC" assigned to Jasper Reid.
